page: Amazon Web Services c8ib.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor running at a clock frequency of 3.9 GHz. Compute resources comprise 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, operating with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The system provides 8.0 GB of total memory, establishing a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core.

Network infrastructure for the c8ib.xlarge delivers a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the instance. The instance does not feature local storage volumes or discrete graphics accelerators. For persistent data operations, workloads must rely on network-attached storage infrastructure. Hardware resource allocation strongly emphasizes CPU execution density over storage and memory footprint.

Given its compute-heavy profile, the instance delivers efficient computational cycles relative to its memory footprint. It is well-aligned with compute-focused tasks such as distributed worker nodes, continuous integration and build systems, web serving, and general batch processing. Tradeoffs include the constrained 8.0 GB RAM capacity and the absence of high-speed local disk storage, which limits suitability for memory-resident datasets or high-IOPS local database systems.
description: Amazon Web Services c8ib.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. Driven by an Intel x86_64 processor running at 3.9 GHz, it supplies 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with dedicated CPU allocation and 2 threads per core. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, producing a 1:2 compute-to-memory profile of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not contain integrated local storage disks or hardware GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage volumes for data persistence. Network interfaces provide a baseline throughput of 4 Gbps. With dedicated high-frequency compute resources and a restrained memory footprint, c8ib.xlarge is designed for CPU-centric tasks including static and dynamic web serving, CI/CD compilation workloads, distributed background processing, and batch compute pipelines that do not demand extensive RAM capacity.
